title: Covalent Bond, Coordinate Covalent Bond and Properties
topicTitle: Covalent bond and coordinate covalent bond; properties of covalent compounds
notes: **Covalent bond:** formed by sharing one or more pairs of electrons between atoms. Usually between non-metals with similar electronegativities.
**Single, double, triple bonds:** sharing 2, 4, or 6 electrons respectively. Bond length decreases and bond strength increases with bond order.
**Coordinate covalent bond (dative bond):** both electrons in the shared pair come from one atom. Example: $NH_3$ donates its lone pair to $BF_3$ to form $H_3N \rightarrow BF_3$.
**Polarity:** if electronegativities differ, the bond is polar with partial charges ($\delta^+$ and $\delta^-$). Equal electronegativities give nonpolar bonds.
**Properties of covalent compounds:** low melting and boiling points (weak intermolecular forces), poor electrical conductivity (no free ions or electrons), often soluble in non-polar solvents.
